name: Scarcity Inventory
description: Hard slot limits with forced triage: when every slot is spoken for, picking something up means choosing what to leave. It wraps inventory.core_inventory rather than replacing it — stacks, item identity, and grants still live there; this owns the cap, the triage prompt, and the drop decision. Item combining to free a slot (herb plus herb) is a recipe concern and stays in inventory.crafting_bench, because a combine button here would re-implement crafting with worse data. The design intent is fixed-inventory horror: the cap must be small enough to force real choices in the first hour, and the triage prompt must show the cost of each choice in one glance — scarcity that requires a spreadsheet reads as tedium, not dread.

inputs.name: maxSlots
inputs.description: Hard cap on carried slots. Eight is the classic survival-horror answer: enough to feel prepared, few enough that the third healing item is a moral decision.

inputs.name: allowStacking
inputs.description: Whether identical stackables share a slot. True by default; the genre's pressure comes from variety decisions (gun or key?), not from counting bullets one slot at a time.

inputs.name: triagePromptOnFull
inputs.description: Whether a pickup into a full inventory opens the triage choice immediately instead of silently refusing. Refusal teaches players to manage space BEFORE picking up, which is the tedium this component exists to avoid.

inputs.name: dropDestroysItem
inputs.description: Whether a triage drop deletes the item or leaves it in the world. False by default — a dropped item you can come back for is a route-planning problem, which is the interesting half of scarcity.

outputs.name: slotsUsed
outputs.description: Occupied slots out of maxSlots. The HUD renders this; AI and loot pacing may read it, but nothing should cache it.

outputs.name: isFull
outputs.description: True when slotsUsed equals maxSlots. The pickup verb checks this and routes to triage instead of failing silently.
